claim.pdf_says: D.19.5.4.2  Class polymorphism  /  D.19.5.4.3  Parametric polymorphism (both fourth-level subclauses of D.19.5.4 Polymorphism, whose first subclause D.19.5.4.1 General is transcribed as '### D.19.5.4.1 General')
claim.markdown_says: ## D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism  ...  ## D.19.5.4.3 Parametric polymorphism
claim.why_it_matters: Both subclauses are emitted at the same markdown level (##) as their own parent '## D.19.5.4 Polymorphism' and one level above their sibling '### D.19.5.4.1 General', so the outline makes them peers of D.19.5.4 instead of its children. Any TOC, anchor-nav or section-scoped tooling over the markdown reports the wrong containment. The transcription's own convention (first sibling nested, later siblings flattened) recurs throughout Annex D - D.18.2.1 is ### while D.18.2.2/D.18.2.3 are ##; D.20.3.1/D.20.3.2 are #### while D.20.3.3/D.20.3.4/D.20.3.5 are ## - which proves the flattening is a tool artifact, not an editorial choice.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is filed as kind='missing-heading', but both headings are present in the transcription, verbatim, correctly numbered, and each carries its derived anchor. Rendered PDF p.1150 prints exactly two bold headings: 'D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism' and 'D.19.5.4.3 Parametric polymorphism'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 46288 reads '## D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism' preceded by '', and line 46317 reads '## D.19.5.4.3 Parametric polymorphism' preceded by ''. Heading text, clause numbers, and body prose all match the page image with no loss. (2) THE PDF HAS NO HEADING LEVEL TO LOSE. I rendered p.1149 to compare siblings across the depth boundary. 'D.19.5.4 Polymorphism' (third level) and 'D.19.5.4.1 General' (fourth level) are printed in IDENTICAL typography - same bold serif face, same point size, same left margin, same spacing - and the p.1150 headings D.19.5.4.2 / D.19.5.4.3 are set in that same identical style. ISO encodes clause hierarchy EXCLUSIVELY through the dotted clause number, not through type size or weight. There is therefore no depth signal in the source document that the markdown could have contradicted. The '##' vs '###' choice is inferred metadata invented by the transcription tool, not transcribed content, so a divergence in it is not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy at all. The containment information the PDF actually carries - the number 'D.19.5.4.2' - is preserved exactly. (3) THE STATED HARM IS ALREADY VOID DOCUMENT-WIDE, SO THIS CHANGES NOTHING. The transcription injects the running page header as an H1 941 times ('# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)') and a page marker as an H2 1261 times ('## Page NNNN') throughout the file. In this very region the sequence is: '### D.19.5.4.1 General' -> '## Page 1150' -> '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' -> '## D.19.5.4.2 Class polymorphism'. Any tool that derives containment from markdown heading depth already reports that every section on p.1150 is a child of a section titled 'Page 1150', and the per-page H1 resets the outline on every one of 941 pages. Markdown heading depth carries no outline semantics anywhere in this file; promoting or demoting these two headings by one level neither creates nor repairs any consumable structure. (4) THE CLAIM'S OWN SUPPORTING PATTERN IS MISSTATED. The asserted convention 'first sibling nested, later siblings flattened' does not hold: D.20.5.1 PRESENT WHEN and D.20.5.2 GROUP INDICATE are BOTH '##', and D.20.6.1/D.20.6.2/D.20.6.3 are ALL '###'. Conversely the anomaly is not confined to later siblings - D.19.5.1 Inheritance is '###' while its own direct sibling D.19.5.4 Polymorphism is '##'. The level assignment is simply noise from the generator, which is precisely why it should not be ledgered as a fidelity defect against the PDF. Per the rejection criteria: the allegedly missing text is present; the difference is formatting only; no meaning changes. real=false.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF/markdown content discrepancy. Both headings are present and verbatim on p.1150 with correct clause numbers and anchors. The finding is really an internal inconsistency in the markdown generator's heading-depth assignment (D.19.5.4.1 emitted at '###' while its siblings D.19.5.4.2/D.19.5.4.3 are emitted at '##'), and the PDF supplies no depth signal to be faithful to - ISO prints D.19.5.4, D.19.5.4.1, D.19.5.4.2 and D.19.5.4.3 in identical bold type, conveying hierarchy solely through the dotted number, which the transcription preserves exactly. The claimed downstream harm cannot occur, because the file already emits an H1 running header 941 times and an H2 'Page NNNN' marker 1261 times, so markdown heading depth is not a usable outline anywhere in the document. If a normalized heading-depth scheme is ever wanted it is a generator cleanup task for the whole file, not a per-page reconciliation defect; the claim's cited convention is also inaccurate (D.20.5.1/D.20.5.2 are both '##'; D.20.6.1-.3 are all '###'; D.19.5.1 is '###' while its sibling D.19.5.4 is '##').
